correctness.rationale: For a current injection at p and extraction at B, the point–block mean drop is 1/(kv). The block equations invert on the separately centered subspaces with scalar denominator k^2-k+lambda=lambda v. The point correction is (k e_p-N e_B)/(lambda v), the block correction (N^T e_p-k e_B)/(lambda v), verifying the transfer-current formula. The negative entries are precisely the disjoint-endpoint cases with one or both cross incidences. Each one-cross class has (k-1)(k-lambda) edges and the two-cross class has (k-1)(lambda-1), by the pair-count identities. Signed column sum one gives the cut norm; the cycle norm changes only the absolute diagonal contribution R=(2v-1)/(kv) to 1-R. The difference of the norms is ((4-k)v-2)/(kv), with the stated strict sign. For a separate upper-bound check, the negative-mass bracket simplifies to 2k-2-2lambda+lambda(lambda+1)/k, less than 2k because lambda+1<=k. Since lambda v>k(k-1), the cut norm is strictly below 5, hence the cycle norm below 6. Substitution of projective-plane parameters gives the displayed expansions and shows sharpness along prime-power orders.
residual_risks: Four recorded exact matrix examples were not rerun; the analytical check is not conditional on them. No existence claim for merely admissible parameter triples or minimum projection constant claim is accepted.
